meetRoy.text:
Hello, I am Roy Dennis M. Patalinghug! I am a 3rd year Filipino student, currently taking Bachelor of Science in Information Technology at the University of San Carlos. 

I love to play video games such as &bMinecraft, Touhou, VALORANT, Roblox, &fand more! I also love to listen to music, and my favorite genres are &aR&&aB, country, rock, and hip-hop. &fSome of my favorite artists are &bDaniel Caesar, Twenty One Pilots, P!ATD, Radiohead, Kenny Rogers, and Arctic Monkeys.

&fWant to know more about me? Go to the next pages to read more about my education and journey to becoming a developer!

My Junior High School and Senior High School were at &bUniversity of San Carlos - North Campus.&f from 2018 until 2024. During those years, I developed my interests in &aprogramming, technology, and computer hardware. &fI was a known computer geek at my class, and I always helped my classmates whenever they were facing tech-related questions.

My college currently is at &bUniversity of San Carlos - Talamban Campus&f, and I'm glad that I am able to finally focus on my passion in becoming a developer in the future.

&cWarning: Long yap session ahead

I started programming back in &b2018 &fbecause of a Minecraft Minigame called &eAnnihilation&f, which inspired me to make my own Minecraft server and recreate their minigame to play with my online friends privately since I didn't have a premium account to join the official server.

I learned &bJava &fas my first programming language through YouTube tutorials and reading many source codes (credits to &bMrLittleKitty in GitHub&f) that helped me create my own plugins for my server and my friends' servers. I also began learning &bMySQL &ffor database management, &bXAMPP &ffor database hosting, &bFileZilla&f for file transferring, and &bGitHub &ffor managing my projects. Overall, these experiences built my tech stack foundation.

I transitioned to Minecraft Bedrock back in &b2020 &fduring the pandemic because not all of my real life friends could run Minecraft Java, and I wanted to play with them on my own server. While searching for server APIs available or bedrock, I discovered &bNukkit&f and started developing entertainment plugins for their small community. 

After learning Nukkit API, my first major plugin I developed was called &eMurderRun, &finspired by SSundee's MurderRun series in YouTube. My goal was to create and promote the minigame that other servers can use through user-friendly configurations and customizations.

I expanded my developer journey in Senior High School where I learned &bFlutter Framework &fthat was used on my research group project called &eHealthink&f. It was the first time that I used a framework and new programming language to create a mobile application, and it took me 1 week to learn the basics and another week to finish the application, thanks to my already established knowledge of coding beforehand.

In college, I learned &bC&f as part of my curriculum in 1st and 2nd year, covering topics such as its fundamentals, and Algorithm and Data Structures. I also had &bWebsite Development &fwhere I learned &bHTML, CSS, JavaScript, and PHP&f. I was the backend developer on majority of website-related projects I've worked with since my designing skill is not the best.

For our &bSystems Integration and Architecture, &fI learned how to use &bSpring Boot &ffor creating backend services, and it uses Java so I was thankful to learn a new framework with my favorite programming language. This is when I made &eMineNets&f cross-platform mobile application as my project for the subject.

For my capstone project that I'll be working on with by group, we decided on proposing a &bWedding Planner Collaboration&f website using &bNext.js, NestJS, and PostgreSQL. &fCurrently, I am learning about &bNext.js and NestJS &ffor 1 month now to prepare myself on developing the website soon.

That's all for now on my little blog, and I will add more content soon given more time in the future. I hope you enjoyed reading my story if you've made it this far. For more information of my projects, visit my GitHub!
